judged_text: In credential-sharing mode the minimumTokenResponseSchema's two computed keys both evaluate to the same literal string (z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() resolve identically), so the z.number() expiry rule is overwritten by z.unknown().optional() and, because zod objects strip unknown keys, safeParse returns only {access_token} — after which line 26 substitutes the literal string 'refresh_token' for the missing refresh_token, and callers persist this stripped object over the stored credential key. office365calendar's refreshAccessToken merges the stripped result over o365AuthCredentials and writes it back via prisma.credential.update (zoom does the same with parsedToken.data), so every refresh while APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED destroys the stored refresh_token (replaced by the placeholder 'refresh_token') and drops the new expiry data. When credential sharing is later switched off, every affected credential holds a garbage refresh_token and can never be refreshed directly again — all affected users must re-authenticate. The original tokens are overwritten with no backup, making the change irreversible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `minimumTokenResponseSchema` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` using computed property keys like `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to fixed literal strings (not dynamic key matching), so the schema effectively only defines `access_token` plus (at best) one nonsensical literal-key field. Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, `safeParse(response)` in credential-sharing mode will drop real fields like `refresh_token` and provider-specific expiry fields. The function then forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" (line `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`). Callers then persist/merge this into stored credentials (e.g., `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` spreads `tokenResponse.data` over `o365AuthCredentials` and writes it via `prisma.credential.update`), overwriting a valid refresh_token with the placeholder and losing expiry data. This is a real data-loss / irreversibility bug when credential sharing is later disabled.
